problem: In multi-target RL, targets that are hard to reach or interact with (e.g., spawned far away) rarely yield successful trajectories, so they are dominated by easy targets in the experience and goal storage and are effectively excluded from learning (Under-explored Target Problem, UTP). Prior multi-task scheduling and curriculum methods need reference scores, extra parameters, or adjustable goals/initial states.
motivation: Real-world service tasks require handling many targets of very different difficulty, and rare or hard targets are also hard for humans to find. Random agents in the Studio-2N 2H map reach 7-8% success on normal targets but only 0.2% on hard targets, so successful experience for hard targets is almost never collected. The paper's observation is that each target's success rate rises at a different time depending on its difficulty, and this signal can drive both sampling and instruction selection without prior knowledge.
key_idea: Form a cycle in which active querying picks instructions for targets under-represented in goal storage, and adaptive sampling focuses the SupCon representation-learning batch on the target whose success rate is rising fastest, using only success-rate and storage statistics.
insight: Adaptive sampling produces an easy-to-hard curriculum, and active querying fills the goal storage for hard targets, which reduces redundant sampling (higher sample richness) for them. Ablation on Studio-2N 2H: GDAN 44.0, adaptive sampling 69.7 vs A5C sampling 56.4 vs uniform 49.6; active querying 65.9 vs A5C querying 57.6; combined 86.6. The combination beats either alone, supporting the claimed virtuous cycle. A5C samples hard targets heavily from the start when their storage is nearly empty, causing redundant sampling.
method: Goal storage + SupCon auxiliary loss: on success, the (goal state, instruction) pair is stored; the feature extractor is trained with SupCon on these pairs, L_total = L_RL + 0.5 L_S, on top of A3C (as in GDAN).

Adaptive sampling: the focused target is argmax_x w_t^x / w_{t-1}^x (largest relative success-rate increase); the batch ratio is B_t(x) = m*1[x = focused] + (1-m)/N with m=0.7, recomputed every 50 updates.

Active querying: the instruction is sampled multinomially from A(x) = softmax over exp(1/(d^x * tau_a)), where d^x is target x's share of goal storage (tau_a=60), so under-represented targets are queried more.
Sample richness metric: M_x/k_x (stored goal states over states sampled for training) used to analyze the cycle.
Setup: warmup with random actions to fill storage (1,000 goal states), 20 A3C processes with shared goal storage, 4-frame 42x42 RGB-D, gated-attention + LSTM.

setting.backbone: A3C with 4-layer CNN feature extractor, gated-attention and LSTM (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Online RL in ViZDoom; up to about 2M updates per run; no extra data
setting.action_space: 3 discrete actions (TurnLeft, TurnRight, GoStraight), each repeated 4 frames
setting.privileged: none (the agent must be able to set its own training instruction; per-target success rates and goal storage are used during training)

numbers.extra: success rate averaged over 500 episodes, at least 5 runs; SEI vs A3C

numbers_note: The Studio (4N) results are given only as a learning curve, not a table. All benchmarks are the authors' own ViZDoom tasks, and 'test' is used as a generic split since there is no official split.
results: L-SA reaches the highest success rate on every UTP task: Studio-2N 2H 86.6% vs A5C 85.4% and GDAN 47.1%, and Studio-6N 74.5% vs A5C 48.5% and GDAN 37.6%. Sample-efficiency improvement is 490% over A3C on Studio-2N 2H and 289.6% over GDAN on Studio-6N. A3C and NGU stay near zero on the harder tasks (6N, 3N 3H, 8N).
limitations: Only applies to tasks with explicit, specific targets; unsuitable when instructions do not name a target (e.g. 'Keep going').
Active querying assumes the agent can set its own training instruction.
Evaluated only on small ViZDoom navigation tasks with 42x42 images and discrete actions; no real-robot or standard benchmark results.
